newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo sets first nationwide credit rating data base.
newsitem.headline: Yugo sets first nationwide credit rating data base.

text.p: Yugoslavia's central bank Accounting and Payments Office presented on Friday its first nationwide credit rating data base offering reliable data to potential investors and creditors.
The first assessment of financial strength of Yugoslav companies and banks, using methodology of Dun & Bradstreet and Robert Morris & Associates, also observes new World Bank and OECD standards.

"The data base will become fully operational by the end of 1997. By the time we will include all relevant information on companies' and banks' performance for 1994, 1995 and 1996," Branko Ljutic, one of the authors of the project, told Reuters.

Ljutic said the first register of transparent financial information, with initial analysis and assessment of creditworthiness of local companies and banks, will be updated once a year and will offer more insight into the entire Yugoslav economy.

"The key aim is to attract investors and creditors and to reduce business risk," Ljutic said and added that the register will be a valuable source of information for all shareholders, financial analysts, managers, employees, creditors, buyers, government and legal bodies.
Information will also be available on Internet.

Both authors and the central bank who ordered the study expected the first credit rating data base to stimulate creation of local credit-reference agencies. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
